{{Short description|Art made with thread strung between points}}
__notoc__
{{More footnotes|date=May 2011}}
[[File:StringArt.jpg|225px|thumb|right|String art, created with thread and paper]]
[[File:E8-with-thread.jpg|thumb|A string art representing a projection of the 8-dimensional [[4 21 polytope|4<sub>21</sub> polytope]]]]
[[File:Quadratic Beziers in string art.svg|thumb|100px|Quadratic Béziers in string art: The end points ('''•''') and control point ('''×''') define the quadratic Bézier curve ('''⋯'''). The arc is a segment of a [[parabola]].]]
'''String art''', '''pin and thread art''', or '''filography''' is characterized by an arrangement of colored thread strung between points to form [[geometric pattern]]s or representational designs such as a ship's [[sail]]s, sometimes with other artist material comprising the remainder of the work. Thread, wire, or string is wound around a grid of nails hammered into a [[velvet]]-covered wooden board. Though straight lines are formed by the string, the slightly different angles and metric positions at which strings intersect gives the appearance of [[Bézier curve]]s (as in the mathematical concept of [[envelope (mathematics)|envelope]] of a family of straight lines). [[Bézier curve#Quadratic curves|Quadratic Bézier curves]] are obtained from strings based on two intersecting segments. Other forms of string art include [[Spirelli]], which is used for [[cardmaking]] and [[scrapbooking]], and curve stitching, in which string is stitched through holes.

String art has its origins in the 'curve stitch' activities invented by [[Mary Everest Boole]] at the end of the 19th century to make mathematical ideas more accessible to children.<ref>{{cite book|contribution=Mary Everest Boole: An Erstwhile Pedagogist for Contemporary Times|title=Vita mathematica|editor1-last=Calinger|editor1-first=Ronald|year=1996|publisher=Cambridge University Press|location=Cambridge|isbn=0-88385-097-4|last=Michalowicz|first=Karen Dee Ann|author-link=Karen Michalowicz|page=291}}</ref> It was popularised as a decorative craft in the late 1960s through kits and books.<ref>{{Cite book|title=String art magic : the secrets to crafting geometric art with string and nail|last=Blanken, Rain, author.|isbn=978-1-940611-73-0|oclc=988301633|date = 2018-06-15}}</ref>

A computational form of string art that can produce photo-realistic artwork was introduced by Petros Vrellis, in 2016.<ref>{{Cite book|title="Beyond the Creative Species: Making Machines That Make Art and Music"|last=Bown|first=Oliver|publisher=The MIT Press|isbn=9780262045018|year=2021}}</ref>
